provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Phonics: i and j words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify i and j words.
The pupils should be able to say i and j words correctly.

Introduction:
We have learned about letters in class.
Today we will learn words with i and j.

Content:
Words with i: ink, iron, iron cloth.
Words with j: jam, jug, jug for water.
Point to pictures as we say the words.

Class activity:
Point to objects in class with i and j sounds.
Say the words together.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does ink make?
Can you find a jug?
What letter is in jam?

Summary:
We can say words with i and j sounds.

topics.title: Phonics: k and l words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify k and l words.
The pupils should be able to say k and l words correctly.

Introduction:
We learned about i and j words last week.
Today we will learn words with k and l.

Content:
Words with k: kite, key, key for door.
Words with l: leg, lion, big lion.
Point to pictures as we say the words.

Class activity:
Point to objects in class with k and l sounds.
Say the words together.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does kite make?
Can you show your leg?
What letter is in lion?

Summary:
We can say words with k and l sounds.

topics.title: Phonics: m and n words
topics.content:

The pupils should be able to say m and n words correctly.

Today we will learn words with m and n.

Words with n: net, nose, nose on face.
Point to pictures as we say the words.

Say the words together.

topics.title: Phonics: o and p words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify o and p words.
The pupils should be able to say o and p words correctly.

Introduction:
We learned about m and n words last week.
Today we will learn words with o and p.

Content:
Words with o: ox, orange, sweet orange.
Words with p: pen, pot, pot for cooking.
Point to pictures as we say the words.

Say the words together.

topics.title: Simple sentences
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read simple sentences.
The pupils should be able to make simple sentences.

Introduction:
We have learned many words in class.
Today we will make sentences with words.

Content:
Simple sentences have few words.
I can run. It is a cup.
Read the sentences together.

Class activity:
Make new sentences with I can.
Read all sentences aloud.

Evaluation questions:
Can you read I can run?
Make a sentence with cup.
What is a simple sentence?

Summary:
We can read and make simple sentences.

topics.title: Rhymes: action songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing action songs.
The pupils should be able to do actions for songs.

Introduction:
We like to sing in class.
Today we will sing with actions.

Content:
Action songs have words and movements.
Sing and act the rhyme.
Clap and move your body.

Class activity:
Stand up and sing with actions.
Clap and move to the beat.

Evaluation questions:
Can you sing the action song?
What action goes with the song?
Do you like action songs?

Summary:
We can sing and do actions for songs.

topics.title: Comprehension: my school
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to talk about school.
The pupils should be able to answer questions.

Introduction:
We come to school every day.
Today we will talk about our school.

Content:
Our school has classrooms and teachers.
We learn and play in school.
Answer questions about school.

Class activity:
Draw your favorite place in school.
Tell the class about your drawing.

Evaluation questions:
What do you do in school?
Who teaches you in school?
What is your favorite place in school?

Summary:
We can talk about our school.

topics.title: Writing: capital letters K to T
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write capital letters K to T.
The pupils should be able to say letter names.

Introduction:
We have learned many letters.
Today we will write capital letters K to T.

Content:
Capital letters are big letters.
Trace and copy K L M N O P Q R S T.
Say each letter as you write.

Class activity:
Write letters in the air with your finger.
Write letters on the board.

Evaluation questions:
Can you write letter K?
What letter comes after P?
How do you write letter T?

Summary:
We can write capital letters K to T.

topics.title: Writing: small letters a to j
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write small letters a to j.
The pupils should be able to match to capitals.

Introduction:
We wrote capital letters last week.
Today we will write small letters a to j.

Content:
Small letters are little letters.
Trace and copy a b c d e f g h i j.
Match small letters to capital letters.

Class activity:
Write letters on sand with sticks.
Match letter cards to pictures.

Evaluation questions:
Can you write small letter a?
What letter comes after f?
Match small b to capital B.

Summary:
We can write small letters a to j.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show what they learned.
The pupils should be able to answer questions.

Introduction:
We have learned many things this term.
Today we will review and check our learning.

Content:
Review all letters and words.
Review simple sentences and songs.
Oral and written quiz.

Class activity:
Play a game with letters and words.
Answer questions about what we learned.

Evaluation questions:
What letters did we learn?
Can you read a simple sentence?
Sing a song we learned.

Summary:
We can show what we learned this term.
